question: In all of the following enzyme deficiencies, hyperammonemia is a common feature, EXCEPT:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency" -> "urea cycle disorder" -> "inability to convert citrulline to argininosuccinate" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase (CPS-I) deficiency" -> "urea cycle disorder" -> "inability to synthesize carbamoyl phosphate from ammonia" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Ornithine Transcarbamoylase (OTC) deficiency" -> "urea cycle disorder" -> "inability to convert ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate to citrulline" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Ornithine Amino Transferase deficiency" -> "gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina" -> "does not involve urea cycle directly" -> "no direct accumulation of ammonia" -> "no hyperammonemia" -> 90%
analysis: The question asks which enzyme deficiency does not commonly feature hyperammonemia. Hyperammonemia is typically associated with defects in the urea cycle, which is responsible for the detoxification of ammonia. Argininosuccinate synthetase, Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase (CPS-I), and Ornithine Transcarbamoylase (OTC) are all enzymes involved in the urea cycle, and deficiencies in these enzymes can lead to hyperammonemia. However, Ornithine Amino Transferase (opd) is involved in the ornithine degradation pathway, not directly in the urea cycle, and its deficiency leads to gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina but not typically to hyperammonemia. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge, Ornithine Amino Transferase deficiency is the correct answer as it is not commonly associated with hyperammonemia.
